HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The SAME shot as the layout reference: same night bank below the palace west wall, same young man in a white sleeping robe dropping into the reeds with his sleeves flying, same composition. CHANGE: no goblins, no smoke hair, no tree man, no rock lady. In their places, poor HUMAN children and an old man in rags wearing carved WOODEN dokkaebi masks, grinning, holding out their arms to catch him, one holding a covered lantern; a rope ladder hangs down the wall. Painted in the house webtoon look, not ink. DEPTH: the subject big and close, razor-sharp, a dark soft out-of-focus foreground shape at the lens, the background the real place painted loosely with colour, weather and haze, big creamy bokeh discs; one hard key carves the faces. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = yongsu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: temp/bh-myth-reeds (the LAYOUT reference (the legend version of this same shot): copy its camera, framing, composition, poses and lighting EXACTLY, the same people in the same places and the same gestures; change ONLY what the scene says is different. Do not copy its faces; faces come from the top row), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). BIHYUNG — Look: Young (as Bihyung, the madman of Surabol): lean, long loose black hair in a careless topknot with ONE stray strand of hair always poking straight up out of it, exactly as on the attached portrait; thin face, quick crooked half-smile. Colour #6a7cb0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
